Prerequisite and/or Corequisite Prerequisite: PH 211, MTH 252 Prerequisite with concurrency: MTH 254 Catalog Course Description Extends and adapts models based on forces and energy to describe and quantify the fundamental physical phenomena of rotational motion, oscillatory motion, collective motion, and optics. Investigates the methods by which physics is built through experiment and observation. Apply Newton’s laws and conservation to analyze the behavior of systems with rotational, oscillatory, or wavelike motion. 2. Construct a variety of representations, including graphs of related motion quantities, extended free-body diagrams, and symbolic equations, and translate from one representation to another. 3. Explain physical behavior based on observations, Newton’s laws, and conservation principles. 4. Investigate the physical world to test models and draw conclusions using the scientific method. 5. Explain how physics principles have led to the development of real-world inventions and devices and how these inventions and devices have impacted society. Your learning will be assessed using a wide variety of assignments. Most assignments in this class are formative. Your responses to the pre-lecture assignments, participation assignments and homework activities will serve a primary formative role in how you learn physics. Your learning will also be assessed by a term project, labs, quizzes and a cumulative final exam for which you will also receive detailed feedback. Expectations for Time and Participation Participation is essential and expected in all components of this course. Attendance in live Zoom lectures is optional, with corresponding asynchronous alternatives available for every synchronous assignment. This course combines approximately 120 total hours of instruction, online activities, and assignments for 4 credits. This means that, according to OSU policy, students are expected to work on course activities (readings, labs, homework, discussions, assessments, etc.) for approximately 12 hours per week in this 4-credit course. Please plan out your schedule to carve out at least 12 hours each week to complete the activities in this course. This course is asynchronous and somewhat flexible, but not self-paced. Our schedule of Course Content and the due dates that appear in Canvas provide guidelines for how you’ll interact and with what frequency. We recommend that you create your own workload schedule and set reminders for assignment due dates. This course is offered through Oregon State University Ecampus. For more information visit: 6 http://ecampus.oregonstate.edu. ## Page 7 Textbook: Most students find it helpful to read the textbook before lecture to help understand what occurs during lecture and ask productive questions. Most students also find it helpful to read the textbook after lecture to solidify what they learned during lecture. Think about the questions asked in the book as you go along and make note of what doesn’t make sense to you so you can ask about it later. Most importantly, don’t fall behind because most concepts build on those encountered earlier. Communication: Communication will be through announcements given in lecture, posted on Canvas, and via email. You are expected to check these daily. Lecture: Lecture meets online via Zoom for one hour, four times per week. The purpose of lecture will be developing conceptual understanding, working on representing phenomenon, practicing problem solving, and building understanding though observations and explanations of phenomena. Lecture is interactive. There will be times in lecture that you are strongly encouraged to talk and work with other students. Questions, comments, and interruptions are welcome, but please virtually raise your hand. Lecture videos will be posted on Canvas, typically within two hours of the lecture. Formative Assessment Points: The Poll Everywhere software will be used for formative assessment during lecture. You are allowed three excused absences (three lowest scores dropped) and still earn the maximum points. The three excused absences cover illness, injury, school events, personal days, weather events, work, technical issues, weather, travel, and any other excused reasons. You can alternatively earn participation points via asynchronous assignments delivered in Canvas. Pre-lecture assignments: Pre-lecture assignments will be open on Canvas for at least 48 hours and will close one hour before class. These assignments will largely be based on assigned textbook reading. Your three lowest scores for pre-lecture assignments will be dropped to cover illness, injury, school events, personal days, weather events, work, technical issues, weather, travel, and any other reasons. Homework: Online homework will be assigned in Canvas. The lowest homework score will be dropped when calculating the total homework score. Lab: Lab is the appropriate place for you to apply the tools and skills to explore more complex situations. The labs will get increasingly more open-ended, so eventually This course is offered through Oregon State University Ecampus. For more information visit: 7 http://ecampus.oregonstate.edu. ## Page 8 you will be able to do authentic physics modeling of real situations. The lab is fully online with TAs available via Zoom. Each group will submit one lab report. Your percentage of earned points will be included in the calculation of your PH 211 grade. You must pass lab to pass the course. You must submit every lab and average at least 70% of the possible points for the lab reports over the course of the term. Late policy: Lab assignments have a 10% deduction per day late, not to go below 50%. Participation assignments have a deduction of one point per day late. Homework assignments have a deduction of 1 point per day late and are not accepted after solutions are posted. Quizzes, final exam, pre-lecture and extra credit assignments are not accepted late. Quizzes and final exam: There will be three quizzes and a comprehensive final exam. All quizzes and the final are closed book and comprehensive, including material from readings, labs, lectures, and/or homework. They will consist of conceptual questions and written-out problems and may include problem solving aspects required for homework, such as producing diagrams and/or graphs, discussing assumptions, concepts, and analysis. One quiz score will be excused to accommodate illness, injury, school events, personal days, work, weather events, technical issues, travel, and any other excused reason. You must submit at least three quizzes to pass the course. A quiz reflection assignment will be given for extra credit for the first two quizzes. Quizzes and the final will be administered in two modalities: proctored via Zoom during the regular class meeting time or at 6pm PDT the same day or an asynchronous alternative. For both modalities, you must have a working web cam. Any student not visible in the web cam during the duration of the quiz will receive a zero for the quiz or exam. The Zoom quiz and final will be administered in Gradescope. The asynchronous quiz and final will be administered via Canvas using Proctorio. The asynchronous questions will be different with the same difficulty level as the Zoom versions, chosen randomly from a question bank in Canvas. For the asynchronous alternative, you need a browser that will support Proctorio and stable internet. If you are dropped from a quiz in Proctorio, it will count as your dropped quiz, and you will be strongly encouraged to attend one of the Zoom meetings for the remaining quizzes. A Proctorio Practice quiz will ensure that you have Proctorio set up correctly before the quiz. You may opt to take a quiz or final exam in an approved testing center. Please contact Ecampus Testing at least two weeks prior to the event and notify the instructor. This course is offered through Oregon State University Ecampus. For more information visit: 8 http://ecampus.oregonstate.edu. ## Page 9 For all quiz and exam modalities, you will be required to sign an integrity statement and submit a scan of an 8.5”x11” notesheet of at least half a page, up to one full page of notes on the current material and your photo ID. The note sheet must be handwritten by you and cannot contain copied images or text or minimized material. Note sheets with AI generated material will not be accepted. No other materials will be allowed during the quiz or exam. Any quiz or exam submitted without an a signed integrity statement and acceptable notesheet with photo ID will receive a score of zero. The note sheet will receive a late deduction of 1 point per day if it is not submitted by the due date/time. Any official quiz conflict must be discussed, and arrangements made with the instructor before the quiz or exam. Unexcused absence will result in a zero for the quiz or exam. If you believe that an error was made in the grading of a question, submit a regrade request in Gradescope within fifteen days after graded submissions are posted on Canvas. Calculators: You will need a calculator for lecture, recitation, lab, and quizzes. If you want to know whether your calculator is acceptable or not for exams, consult the instructor before the first quiz. Incomplete: To qualify for a grade of Incomplete, you must be missing one major assignment at most (one lab, for example) and be otherwise passing the class with at lease a C-. You need to request an Incomplete from the instructor before the end of the term.
